meta.name: David Samtani
meta.title: From a Minimal Inference Server to Production Engines: vLLM and Mooncake
meta.device: NVIDIA A10 (24 GB) · Lambda Cloud · driver 580.126.20 / CUDA 13.0

source.harness: code/run_sweep.py drives code/minimal_full_server.py in-process (minimal_b1) and vLLM's streaming /v1/completions endpoint (vllm_paged, mooncake, mooncake_warm). Servers are launched by code/lambda/run_all.sh, run_mooncake.sh, run_wildchat.sh. Synthetic prompts come from PromptBuilder in run_sweep.py (fixed FILLER text, repeated then truncated until the chat-templated prompt hits the exact target length). WildChat prompts come from wildchat_prompts() in the same file. vLLM 0.32.0, torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.19.0, mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.13.post1.

workload.notes: The synthetic grid (used in both plots) is a fixed English filler passage trimmed so the TinyLlama chat-templated prompt is exactly 128 / 512 / 1984 tokens (1984 + 64 new = the 2048-token context limit), prefixed with a unique tag per request so no two requests share a full prompt. The same generator feeds every system. The WildChat sanity check (rows with prompt_source = "wildchat", excluded from the plots) uses the first 20 English, non-toxic first user turns of allenai/WildChat-1M (data/train-00000-of-00014.parquet, file order) with 16-1984 templated tokens, 1 warm-up + 3 reps at N = 1 and 4. prompt_tokens on those rows is the median across the burst. All systems use temperature 0, ignore_eos, exactly 64 new tokens, one untimed warm-up burst per cell, and N clients released together by a barrier. TTFT = request start to first streamed token (includes queueing, since the baseline serves a burst sequentially and its TTFT includes waiting for earlier requests). TBT = gaps between streamed tokens, p50 and mean per client. KV bytes = dense formula kv_bytes(22 layers, 4 KV heads, seq_len, head_dim 64, 2 bytes) at seq_len = prompt + new - 1, not the engine's allocated pool. mooncake_warm sends each burst once untimed and then times an identical resend. vLLM's own prefix cache is disabled for both Mooncake runs, so warm hits come only from the Mooncake store (the vLLM log shows an external prefix-cache hit rate of up to 46%). One caveat is that prompts of the same length share their first ~16 tokens (chat template + tag stem), so one 16-token KV block can be reused even in cold runs. This affects vllm_paged and mooncake equally and is under 1% of a 1984-token prompt.

systems.label: minimal_full_server (batch = 1)
systems.description: code/minimal_full_server.py imported in-process, running HF transformers in fp16 (no quantization) with a DynamicCache on the GPU, one request at a time. A burst of N is served sequentially, so client k waits for k-1 full generations.
systems.novelty: Contiguous per-request KV cache with no batching or scheduler. This is the reference every other system improves on.

systems.label: vLLM (PagedAttention + continuous batching)
systems.description: vllm serve TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 with default settings (bf16 weights and KV, no quantization, prefix caching and chunked prefill on, CUDA graphs) and a streaming /v1/completions client.
systems.novelty: PagedAttention keeps KV in fixed-size blocks, and continuous (iteration-level, Orca-style) batching admits new requests every step, so N = 4 requests prefill and decode together instead of queueing.

systems.label: vLLM + Mooncake store (cold)
systems.description: Same vLLM server (bf16) with --kv-transfer-config MooncakeStoreConnector (kv_role kv_both), a local mooncake_master and a 16 GB embedded store over TCP. vLLM's prefix cache is disabled. Every request is new, so lookups miss and every KV is written to the store.
systems.novelty: A hash-addressed KV pool outside the GPU. KV blocks are saved to a shared store keyed by prefix hash. Cold runs pay the save cost with nothing to reuse.

systems.label: vLLM + Mooncake store (warm prefix)
systems.description: Same server as mooncake. Each burst is sent once untimed, then the identical prompts are timed, so their KV is already in the store.
systems.novelty: Prefix reuse means KV for an already-seen prefix is fetched from the Mooncake store instead of recomputed, which should cut prefill time more as prompts get longer.

takeaways: Batching is the big win under load: at N = 4 the baseline queues requests, so its median TTFT is ~1.5 s and the last client waits 3.0-3.4 s, while vLLM serves the same burst in 26 / 72 / 191 ms (128 / 512 / 1984-token prompts).
vLLM decodes ~2.9x faster per user (TBT 5.5-6.0 ms vs ~15.8 ms for the HF baseline), and its TBT rises only 0.1-0.4 ms from N = 1 to N = 4, so batching costs decode almost nothing at this scale.

Mooncake prefix reuse pays off on long prompts: at 1984 tokens warm TTFT is 43 ms vs 77 ms cold (N = 1) and 142 ms vs 377 ms cold (N = 4), beating plain vLLM (73 / 191 ms) with a lower tail (p95 182 vs 299 ms).

Reuse is not free: cold Mooncake is slower than plain vLLM under load (377 vs 191 ms at 1984 tokens, N = 4) because every KV is also written to the store, and on short real WildChat prompts warm is no better than cold (N = 4 median 31 vs 23 ms).

KV bytes are identical across systems (46.1 MB at 1984 + 63 tokens) because they come from the dense formula. The systems differ in where that KV lives (contiguous tensor, paged blocks, external store), not in its size.
summary: I compared a minimal single-request Hugging Face server (minimal_full_server) with vLLM and with vLLM + Mooncake's KV store (cold and warm prefix) serving TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat on one NVIDIA A10 (Lambda Cloud), sweeping 128 / 512 / 1984-token prompts x 1 and 4 concurrent clients x 3 reps with 64 new tokens, plus a 20-prompt WildChat-1M sanity check. At N = 1 every system is fast (TTFT 12-92 ms) and the gap is mostly kernel efficiency. At N = 4 scheduling dominates. The baseline's TTFT is pure queueing (~1 s per earlier request), while vLLM's continuous batching keeps all four clients within ~300 ms even at 1984 tokens and holds TBT near 6 ms. Mooncake's novelty shows up only in TTFT and only when there is a long prefix to reuse. Warm nearly halves TTFT at 1984 tokens, but cold runs pay a store-write overhead and short chat prompts see no gain.
